newsitem.title: TANZANIA: S.Africa Breweries sees Tanzania sales up.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Breweries sees Tanzania sales up.

text.p: South Africa Breweries Ltd's sales in Tanzania are forecast to rise 35 percent in 1996 and the company is optimistic about sales potential, according to a senior manager.
"Our sales have so far this year increased 35 percent from 1995," Danie Niemandt, chief exective director for SAB in Tanzania, said at the weekend.

SAB, biggest shareholder in Tanzania Breweries Ltd, has invested $28 million in the company in which it holds a 46 percent share. The Tanzania government holds 41 percent and two private banks hold remaining shares.

"We started operating (in Tanzania) in 1993 when sales reached just over 495,000 hectolitres. In 1994 that increased to 620,000 hectolitres and to about 870,000 in 1995. This year, we will sell about 1.2 million hectolitres," Niemandt said.

Tanzania Breweries Ltd launched Kilamanjaro in October in addition to Safari Lager, a beer that sells volumes equivalent to 70 percent of Tanzania's estimated beer market of 1.7 million hectolitres, he said.
Kenya Breweries Ltd's Tusker Lager takes the biggest remaining share while another local brand Serengeti and foreign brands acount for some five percent.
"I think it has been very successful, it's already now starting to live up to expectations 12 to 18 months ahead of planning," he told Reuters in an interview.
Per capita beer consumption stands at five litres per capita per year, though the market could grow to 2.5 million hectolitres over five years.
SAB invested $17.5 million of its $28 million total in Tanzania in 1996. A further $11 million investment is planned for 1997.
